_comment: Harness defaults; personal overrides go in settings.local.json (gitignored). `model` + `effortLevel` mirror config models.session {model, effort} (/harness-doctor check 10 checks agreement); CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL and `claude --effort` override effortLevel at launch. /harness-init appends the project's gate commands to permissions.allow (headless -p runs auto-deny anything non-allowlisted). The five guard hooks come from the installed lean-agent-harness plugin, not this repo. Why there are no deny rules on config/specs writes, and why hooks are a denylist not a sandbox: docs/sandboxing.md. The `codex --sandbox read-only` entry (2026-09-09) exists because models.review.second routes to the Codex CLI and /review dispatches it through the Bash tool: without it a headless `claude -p "/review"` auto-denies the second judge, which has no fallback and so fails closed to REJECT on every run. It is deliberately NOT `Bash(codex:*)` — the engine's arg builder emits `--sandbox <mode>` as argv[0], so this prefix admits read-only judge runs only and a workspace-write codex run still prompts. The loop path is unaffected either way: loop.sh spawns codex itself, outside the permission system.
_worktree_note: One session = one worktree (AGENTS.md 'Session isolation' + CLAUDE.md 'Claude Code specifics'). baseRef 'fresh' branches each session's worktree from origin's default branch (clean tree matching the remote); 'head' would carry local unpushed state. .claude/settings.json, permissions, the plugin, and .git/hooks all resolve through a worktree to the main checkout, so the guard hooks + pre-commit privacy guard apply inside it for free.
